newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice to investigate INS citizenship program.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice to investigate INS citizenship program.

text.p: The Justice Department's inspector general said Monday an investigation will be conducted into the Immigration and Naturalisation Service's controversial "Citizenship USA" programme.

Inspector General Michael Bromwich said the investigation would examine allegations of mismanagement, misconduct and illegality in the programme in which more than a million people became citizens between September 1995 and October 1996.

Republicans in Congress have charged that proper procedures were not followed and that applicants in the programme had been rushed through so they could vote for Democrats in last November's elections.

They have asked Attorney General Janet Reno to appoint an independent counsel to investigate the various allegations, including whether Vice President Al Gore's office played a key role in the initiative. But Reno has rejected the request.

"The investigation will go wherever the facts lead us," Bromwich said, adding: "We will reconstruct the story of how (the program) was developed and implemented and the respects in which it may have gone off the rails."

Republicans in Congress have criticised the immigration service for granting citizenship last year to thousands of unqualified aliens, including some with criminal records, because of poor background checks.
Bromwich said the investigation will focus on the development of the initiative at immigration service headquarters and the way field offices carried it out.

He said the probe will look at the activities of immigration offices in Miami, New York, Chicago, Los Angeles and San Francisco, cities which accounted for the vast majority of the 1.3 million approved citizenships.
